record.title: FARMS links source-contextual Lean statements to bounded numerical skills
record.summary: FARMS is an author-reported pipeline that links mathematical source context and computational meaning to Lean statements, then uses semantic review, bounded repair and abstention alongside compilation. In 171 selected randomized-linear-algebra and numerical-PDE targets, the authors report 157 accepted outcomes, including three with source warnings. Two small numerical applications use selected statements in heat-flow solving and wave-response compression. A six-target comparison reports lower per-target costs than the authors’ statement-level AutoformBot adaptation, but that comparison allowed sorry for target and auxiliary proofs and is restricted to this configuration. The paper does not establish independent replication, broad domain transfer, proof-complete corpus coverage or automated discovery of new methods.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: arXiv identifies FARMS as a v1 paper submitted by Di Wu, Ling Liang and Haizhao Yang on 2026-10-29.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across 171 selected targets from four sources in randomized numerical linear algebra and numerical PDEs, the authors report 157 accepted pipeline outcomes: 154 without source warnings and three with explicit source warnings. Acceptance means VERIFIED_PASS or COMPILED_WITH_SOURCE_WARNING; it is not an independent judgment that every source theorem or translation is correct.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For six randomly selected targets, the authors’ statement-level AutoformBot adaptation reports $2.84 per target for FARMS versus $58.02 for AutoformBot. The comparison restricted both systems to the selected statements, allowed sorry in target and auxiliary proofs for AutoformBot, and required execution/interface changes; it is not a general proof-complete cost comparison.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors demonstrate two bounded applications using source-linked Lean statements and connecting proofs: six prescribed heat-flow runs met a discrete energy-error target of 10^-6, while three prescribed wave-response seeds reduced a 32-time response library from 24 MiB to 8.375 MiB under a stated 0.01 energy-error bound for a fixed excitation family.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper describes separate source-context review, Lean compilation, semantic review, bounded repair and abstention. Its worked examples report recovery of omitted mathematical conditions and detection of a source optimality claim missing a positive-sampling assumption.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish independent reproducibility, broad transfer across mathematical disciplines or recent research literature, proof-complete formalization at the reported pipeline acceptance rate, or autonomous discovery of new numerical methods. The authors identify wider source coverage, cross-textbook integration and new-method discovery as open work.

evidence_gaps.description: This activation did not inspect the paper-linked repository, pin a build environment or independently compile selected statements and connecting proofs.
Transfer beyond four sources/two mathematical areas and the six-target adapted AutoformBot cost comparison are not independently established.

brief.importance_rationale: If independently extended, source-grounded formal representations that retain algorithms and quantitative conditions could support safer reuse of mathematical methods in computational science; current scope is four sources in two areas and two bounded numerical applications.
limitations: All quantitative outcomes are reported by the paper authors; no independent reproduction or Lean build was performed.
The corpus covers 171 selected statements from four sources in randomized numerical linear algebra and numerical PDEs, not broad scientific disciplines or contemporary research literature.
The 157 accepted outcomes include three source-warning cases; acceptance may be VERIFIED_PASS or COMPILED_WITH_SOURCE_WARNING and is not equivalent to independent validation of the source theorem.
The six-target AutoformBot comparison is a constrained statement-level adaptation permitting sorry in target and auxiliary proofs; it is not a proof-complete or general cost comparison.

The heat-flow and wave-response applications are bounded, author-run examples on prescribed numerical problems and seed sets; general scientific-agent utility and discovery of new methods remain open.
brief.summary: FARMS is an author-reported pipeline that links mathematical source context and computational meaning to Lean statements, then uses semantic review, bounded repair and abstention alongside compilation. In 171 selected randomized-linear-algebra and numerical-PDE targets, the authors report 157 accepted outcomes, including three with source warnings. Two small numerical applications use selected statements in heat-flow solving and wave-response compression. A six-target comparison reports lower per-target costs than the authors’ statement-level AutoformBot adaptation, but that comparison allowed sorry for target and auxiliary proofs and is restricted to this configuration. The paper does not establish independent replication, broad domain transfer, proof-complete corpus coverage or automated discovery of new methods.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report 157 accepted pipeline outcomes among 171 selected targets; costs estimated at $0.85–$2.29 per planned target across four source collections; and $2.84 versus $58.02 per target on six randomly selected targets against a restricted statement-level AutoformBot adaptation.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected paper describes source retrieval/audit, Lean statement construction, compilation, semantic review, repair and abstention. In two bounded author-run applications, selected formal statements support numerical parameter or accuracy decisions. No independent build or experiment was performed.
technical.mechanism: Source packages retain definitions, assumptions, algorithm descriptions and passage evidence. Formalizers create Lean statements; a semantic referee checks objects, assumptions, quantifiers, algorithms and guarantees beyond compilation. Findings enter bounded repair or abstention. Selected source propositions are then connected by Lean-checked implications to numerical procedures.
technical.regime: 171 selected statements from four sources in randomized numerical linear algebra and numerical PDEs; two bounded numerical applications; one six-target statement-level cost comparison. The authors use Claude Code with claude-opus-5-5 for principal review/formalization roles.
technical.reproducibility: The arXiv v1 full text is accessible. The linked repository and formalization artifacts were not inspected in this activation, and no code, Lean build or numerical experiment was executed. Results remain author-reported.
technical.strongest_baseline: The six-target cost comparison uses an author-adapted AutoformBot statement-level workflow with the same source documents, but allows sorry for target and auxiliary proofs and includes execution/model-interface changes. It does not establish a broad matched comparison against proof-complete formalization.

brief.title: FARMS links source-contextual Lean statements to bounded numerical skills
brief.why_it_matters: If extended and independently checked, source-contextual formal representations that preserve applicability conditions and quantitative guarantees could help numerical agents reuse mathematical methods more safely. The current evidence is a single paper across four sources in two areas, with two bounded applications and author-reported costs.
